analysis: The supplied changes are confined to the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. Production code is not modified. The changed ranges are: StubTokenizer gains a `decodeTable` (head lines 146-147, 155); `makeBridge` gains a `stopStringScope` parameter that is forwarded to EngineV2Bridge (head lines 443, 462); and new tests are added around head lines 847-899. The patch excerpt is truncated, so those new tests are only partly visible. They appear to cover `EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence` with a ReasoningStopScope. Base units 6 and 7 are unchanged test context. They exercise the SSD prefix cache (T-041): resident-vs-SSD tier choice, receipt isolation across scopes (`scope-a` and `scope-b`), and cleanup of staged bytes. Head unit 8 covers bridge tests for complete-checkpoint pump receipt ownership and donation demand hints. None of these test changes weaken a security control or add attack surface. They add coverage for cache-scope isolation and receipt cleanup, which supports the T-041 mitigations. Test-only changes do not alter the SSD cache TTL, key derivation, scope derivation or production gates. The stop-string scoping change is a correctness feature, not a trust-boundary change. I could not verify that the production `stopStringScope` and `matchedStopSequence` implementation is correct, because that source was not supplied. This is a coverage limit rather than evidence of a flaw. Integration should confirm that EngineV2Bridge.swift changes, if any are in other batches, preserve receipt and cacheScope isolation.
